_readme: OUTBOUND PLAYBOOK — steers how the agent drafts cold outreach. Hand-edit as your outbound strategy evolves. Claims still come ONLY from product-truth.json; this file governs structure/tone, not what's true about the product.

touch1.goal: Open a conversation with a specific, provable observation about THIS prospect — not a pitch. Earn a reply, not a booking.
structure: Reference the real signal about them (their public WhatsApp number, a slow-reply review, a job listing, their destination). Never a templated opener with only [Company] swapped in.
Ask one concrete question about their quoting workflow (e.g. when a group size changes mid-thread, is re-pricing automatic or a manual re-quote?).
One sentence of credibility: built by an Egypt operator after 30+ years, reads the WhatsApp thread and re-prices automatically.
A soft, low-pressure offer — a 5-minute look with their own kind of booking — NOT a hard Calendly link on the first touch.
touch1.length: Short — 60–110 words. Plain text, like a real person typed it. No marketing gloss, no bullet lists, no images.
touch1.subject: Lowercase, specific, non-salesy (e.g. 'your whatsapp quoting'). No emojis, no ALL CAPS, no 'Re:' tricks.

touch2.goal: Proof, not pressure. A short follow-up on the same thread that shares ONE concrete result and gently re-raises the touch-1 question.
structure: Reply on the same thread (reference your first note briefly).
Share one operator's result as proof, honestly caveated (e.g. Travel2Egypt went from 3–4 hours per itinerary to ~5 minutes — not claimed as universal).
Tie it back to the pain you named in touch 1.
No hard ask; a soft 'if that's a live pain point' close.
touch2.subject: Reuse the touch-1 subject (same thread) — the system prepends 'Re:'.

touch3.goal: Permission to close the loop. A polite final note that leaves the door open without guilt.
structure: Acknowledge the timing may be off — no pressure.
Leave the demo link available for whenever quoting speed or margin visibility becomes a priority: https://calendly.com/autoura
touch3.subject: Reuse the touch-1 subject (same thread).

voice: Operator-to-operator. Warm, direct, concrete. Sounds like Islam wrote it, not a marketing team.
must_do: Reference the prospect's specific signal — if no signal is provided, keep the observation honest and general to their destination rather than inventing specifics.
Only make claims grounded in product-truth.json. Caveat QuickBooks/Xero as 'in beta, push-only'. Never quote a price outside the four tiers.
Be honest about non-Egypt destinations (you load your own rates from a blank table).
must_not: Never invent facts about the prospect you weren't given.
Never make a claim not in product-truth.json.
Never put a hard Calendly link or a demo booking as the touch-1 call to action — that's for warm replies.
No pushy urgency, no fake scarcity, no 'just following up' guilt.
Never contact via WhatsApp cold — email/LinkedIn only (enforced by the system, but never draft copy that implies WhatsApp outreach).
signals_to_reference: Public WhatsApp Business number on their site/booking page
Manual PDF itineraries with inconsistent branding
TripAdvisor/Google reviews mentioning slow quotes or price changing after booking
Expanding into a new destination (Jordan, Morocco)
